title: Péter Horváth
text:
POLICY ECONOMIST · EMPIRICAL MACROECONOMICS

I am a Research Economist at the Ministry of Finance of Hungary and a PhD Candidate in Economics at Corvinus University of Budapest. My work combines empirical macroeconomics, monetary policy, forecasting and econometric modelling to study how policy intervention and macro-financial shocks shape the economy.

title: Péter Horváth
text:
Policy & research


My main professional focus is applied macroeconomics: building evidence and quantitative tools that can inform policy questions.
My academic work complements policy-oriented work, with research on monetary transmission, macro-financial interactions, uncertainty and the distributional effects of policy. In my current role, I work on the macro-modelling and forecasting toolkit of the Macro Division at the Ministry of Finance.




01

Monetary policy
Transmission, forward guidance and state dependence.



02

Macroeconomic modelling
Forecasting, scenario analysis and nonlinear dynamics.



03

Applied econometrics
Bayesian methods, nonlinear models and data-driven research.

DISSERTATION · CHAPTER 1

PUBLISHED · 2026

title: CV
text:
Profile
I am a research economist working at the intersection of applied macroeconomics, empirical research and quantitative policy analysis. My PhD research studies nonlinear monetary-policy transmission using modern time-series and Bayesian econometric methods. My current work focuses on macroeconomic modelling, forecasting and scenario analysis.

title: Research
text:
Dissertation



PHD DISSERTATION · CORVINUS UNIVERSITY OF BUDAPEST


Essays on the Nonlinear Transmission of Monetary Policy
My dissertation studies how the transmission of monetary policy varies across economic states, uncertainty regimes and dimensions of the yield curve.


Full dissertation ↗


Chapter 1 — Monetary Transmission in a Fragmented Uncertain World



CONFERENCE-READY · WITH TOHID ATASHBAR


Monetary Transmission in a Fragmented Uncertain World
How economic uncertainty affects monetary policy transmission. Using Bayesian threshold VARs across 30 economies, the paper finds that inflation responds markedly less to monetary shocks in high-uncertainty states while the GDP response remains comparatively stable.


PDF ↗



Chapter 2 — Housing-market imbalances and monetary transmission



PUBLISHED · 2026


Nonlinear Transmission of Monetary Policy and Housing Market Imbalances: Evidence From a Factor-Augmented Threshold VAR Analysis
Housing-market conditions affect both monetary-policy behaviour and the transmission of monetary shocks. Evidence from the United States points to more gradual policy easing around housing booms and somewhat stronger contractions in activity and financial aggregates.


Journal ↗



Chapter 3 — Forward guidance and the yield curve



CONFERENCE-READY


A Distributional Perspective on Forward Guidance and the US Term Structure
Monetary policy announcements affect conditional volatility as well as the conditional mean of the US yield curve. Standard policy-rate shocks tend to increase volatility, while forward guidance compresses it, however, the volatility effects are smaller and less persistent than the mean effects.


PDF ↗
